name: Villagers Work Their Own Job First
description: Villagers practise their selected job on their own: about three times in four, each time the game chooses what a villager does, a villager whose selected job is Farming, Research, Healing or Building, or Devotion (Devotion while you play only when Easier Devotee Training is not selected, so the two never double up) first tries that job's own work, at any food level; the rest of the time, and whenever there is nothing of theirs to do, the game chooses exactly as it always has. The one roll is shared with Builders Fix Huts When Idle, so a choice is either all patched or all stock. What the work is -- which crop, project, patient or study -- is the game's own choice, with its own technology levels and buildings, so nothing starts that the game itself would not allow. As in the game, a villager goes to their job on their own only above skill 5 -- in every game: in A New Home the game sent them from skill 2, and now waits for 6 as the other games do. Researchers never take the place of a farming attempt, and Parenting is left to the game and the Birth Control patches. **This patch never sends a builder to start a project nobody was ever dropped on; it only puts builders first to carry on work that was started**. Healers heal the sick, or study medicine once the Pain Totem has been dismantled. **This patch also turns off the game's "untrained" mark.** In the stock game a villager who has never been dropped on a job does no work on their own at all, however skilled (a child who grew up with skills, for example, just stands around at 14). With this patch every adult 14 or older works on their own as in Virtual Villagers 1-3: the game picks their best skill (or their checked job most of the time) and goes to it only above skill 5, and then only (skill + 40) times in 100, so a skilled villager works often and a beginner still idles. Mating is never put first and stays under the game and the Birth Control patches. The mark is kept in the save, so without this patch the game behaves as it always has. Heathens get nothing new. In catch-up a farmer may also harvest noni before the Hungry Totem is dismantled, as a farmer you dropped there already does. This also applies during catch-up -- the time that passes while the game is closed, and Time Warp. Catch-up's low-food rule still wins: at 250 food or less a villager with Farming 20 or more farms, whatever their job. An addendum to Builders Fix Huts When Idle. **Requires Builders Fix Huts When Idle**, whose DLL loads this one (in The Secret City, a small stub in the page the Origins-exclusive base appends does); ticking this ticks it, and it brings with it the Origins-exclusive base, which adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens.
behavior_changes: Whenever the adult scheduler (or the catch-up worker's pick dispatch, 0x46E9C9 returning to 0x46E9CE) asks the work dispatcher to start a job, for a villager whose selected job is Farming, Research, Healing or Building or Devotion (Farming 0, Parenting 1, Healing 2, Research 3, Building 4, Devotion 5), the dispatcher is first asked for that villager's own job; if that starts something the caller sees it started, and if there is nothing of theirs to do the caller's own request runs unchanged. Parenting is never put first. Research never displaces a Farming request.

About three times in four, not always: the companion asks the decision's roll that Builders Fix Huts When Idle draws once per choice of the idle scheduler and once per run of the catch-up worker (VvfpFixHutsRoll, handed over through VvfpWorkFirstSetRoll, or looked up by module name in The Secret City); when it fails, the caller's own request runs alone, exactly as the stock game.
Builders never start a project nobody was dropped on: New Believers' Building case only continues projects above 0%, so a builder is always put first.
Only above skill 5 (the owner, 2026-11-18): a villager is never put first while their skill in that job is 5 or less, as every game's job picker never sends them (its own gate, cmp esi, 5).

Devotion (job 5) is put first like Healing: in catch-up always; while you play only when Easier Devotee Training's bytes are not at 0x46F1DD (stock 83B9FC1C00000D7554), so the two never double up. The dispatcher's Devotion case (0x46CDB6) queues Honoring when project 14 is complete or 0x4271C0 answers 1 or 2, and otherwise starts nothing.

Untrained mark off (the owner, 2026-11-19): every new villager starts with [record+0x1C54] = 1 (0x4687D3), and the dispatcher refuses every job while it is 1 (0x46C565) -- its only gate; the scheduler's and worker's assigned-site tests (0x46F240, 0x46E96B) and the end-of-action resets (0x452D15, 0x455235, 0x465D2B) treat 1 as nothing assigned. Every request of the scheduler (returns 0x46F291, 0x46F2D6, 0x46F2EA) and of the catch-up worker (0x46E9CE, and the low-food Farming dispatch 0x46E9B1) is dispatched with the mark set to 0 for that call and put back to 1 afterwards if it is still 0 (a refusal inside the call writes 0); the job is the stock picker's (0x46A3C0: above skill 5, then (skill + 40)%), Parenting only when it picks it.
Heathens (u8 record+0x1CEC non-zero) get nothing new: the dispatcher hook, the untrained mark and the noni offer all leave them to the stock game.
At 250 food or less a healer's pick is also dispatched at once instead of waiting behind a farming attempt, as Builders Fix Huts When Idle already does for builders.
explicit_non_changes: This row changes no executable bytes: the fix-huts companion loads the DLL, which detours the sites below at run time, all of them or none, only after verifying the stock bytes; a different build of the game installs nothing.

A villager with nothing of their own to do does whatever the stock scheduler chose; the younger villagers' routine, every other caller of the dispatcher and a villager with no selected job are untouched.
Parenting (job 1) is never put first, and the catch-up worker's Parenting pick (its 5% conception attempt) is not touched: births stay under the Birth Control patches.

What the work does -- which crop, project, hut, patient or study -- is the game's own dispatcher's choice, with its technology levels and buildings; the Farming cases start no tool or sack job (those stay drop-only) and no puzzle work.

In catch-up, the worker's low-food Farming dispatch (0x46E9AC: 250 food or less and Farming 20 or more) never puts anyone's own job first, so Farming wins exactly as in the stock game; the hook only ignores the untrained mark for it.
Nothing is written to the save or any file. The only record write is the untrained mark, lifted for one dispatch and put back, so the save keeps it.

runtime_detours.routine: the work dispatcher's entry, acting only for the adult scheduler's calls (returns 0x46F291, 0x46F2D6, 0x46F2EA) and the catch-up worker's pick dispatch (0x46E9CE); for the worker's low-food Farming dispatch (0x46E9B1) it only ignores the untrained mark

the Farming case's catch-up test before noni (cmp byte [game+0x17E10], bl; jne): in catch-up a villager whose selected job is Farming is offered noni on the decision's roll, before the Hungry Totem as a dropped farmer already is
